body:
Apologies if this has come up before (couldn't see anything in the issues tracker) but has there been any attempt to try and provide relative weighting/importance for controls for companies that are pre-L1? I know that there is the "o" recommended controls concept but that is still a little binary.

For example, I would rather that a company focused on [5.3.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x13-V5-Input-Validation.md#53-injection-prevention-requirements) as opposed to [2.4.7](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v24-memorized-secrets-authenticator-requirements) but they are both currently on an equal footing.

comments.body: There hasn't and there should be, I'm just honestly not sure on the best way to approach this. Any suggestions? weighting is often a subjective topic

So my understanding is that L1 is "[the bare minimum that all applications should strive for](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x03-Using-ASVS.md#level-1-opportunistic)".

Maybe you could have a L0 or L0.5 which represents a subset of L1 items which an organisation should start with whilst on their way to L1, using ```✓``` for where to start and ```o``` for the next most important. It isn't the most elegant solution but at least it is relatively simple :) I think it also provides some form of priority whilst also making it clear that below L1 is not considered an appropriate security level.
I am going to close this as it looks like #350 will decide this.

title: Weighting/importance/low hanging fruit
